channel.title: Legacy Medical Journal
channel.description: Health notes from Legacy Medical, a concierge internal medicine practice in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

item.title: Strength training after 50: why muscle matters as you age
item.description: Muscle strength shapes how well you age. What the federal guidelines recommend, what the research shows, and how to start lifting safely after 50.

item.title: Body composition vs. BMI: what the scale misses
item.description: BMI is a quick screening number, not a verdict. What it cannot tell you about fat, muscle and where weight sits, and better questions to ask as you age.

item.title: VO2 max: why fitness may predict a longer life
item.description: Cardiorespiratory fitness is one of the strongest predictors of how long people live. What VO2 max means, what the studies show, and how to improve yours.

item.title: How sleep changes with age, and what helps
item.description: Older adults still need seven to nine hours of sleep, but sleep changes with age. Insomnia, sleep apnea, and the evidence-based fixes worth asking about.

item.title: Coronary artery calcium scoring: who it helps
item.description: A coronary calcium scan can sharpen a borderline heart risk estimate. Who guidelines say it helps, what the score means, and when it adds little.

item.title: ApoB and lipoprotein(a): cholesterol numbers worth asking about
item.description: Beyond LDL: what apolipoprotein B and lipoprotein(a) measure, why Lp(a) is worth checking once, and how these numbers can change a heart-risk plan.

item.title: Prediabetes and A1c: how to turn the numbers around
item.description: An A1c of 5.7 to 6.4 percent means prediabetes. What that number measures, why the evidence for lifestyle change is strong, and what to do next.

item.title: GLP-1 medications for weight: what to know before you ask
item.description: Semaglutide and tirzepatide changed weight treatment. What the trials showed, common side effects, what happens when you stop, and questions to ask first.

item.title: Menopause and heart health: why midlife is the time to pay attention
item.description: Heart disease is the leading cause of death for women, and risk rises after menopause. What changes, which numbers to watch, and where hormones fit.

item.title: Bone density screening: who needs it, women and men
item.description: Osteoporosis is silent until a bone breaks. Who should have a DXA scan, what the T-score means, how often Medicare covers it, and why men count too.

item.title: Midlife blood pressure and brain health
item.description: High blood pressure in midlife is linked to memory problems later. What the SPRINT MIND trial found, and why steady control protects the brain.

item.title: Skin cancer checks for Florida residents
item.description: Skin cancer is the most common cancer in the US, and Florida sun adds up. How to check your own skin, what to watch for, and when to see a dermatologist.

item.title: Alcohol after 50: what the newer guidance says
item.description: The 2025 to 2030 Dietary Guidelines dropped daily drink limits and simply advise drinking less. Why alcohol affects you differently after 50, and what to ask.

item.title: Balance and fall prevention: staying steady after 60
item.description: More than one in four older adults falls each year, and most falls are preventable. The risk factors, the exercises that work, and what your doctor can check.

item.title: Hearing loss, hearing aids and memory
item.description: Hearing loss is common after 60 and linked to faster cognitive decline. What the ACHIEVE trial found, over-the-counter hearing aids, and what Medicare covers.

item.title: A longevity plan for the year ahead, built with your internist
item.description: Longevity medicine is mostly the basics done well and followed over time. A year-round plan built around your annual physical, without the hype.

item.title: Can you pay concierge fees from an HSA or FSA?
item.description: A 2026 IRS rule lets HSAs pay some direct primary care fees. Why concierge fees may not qualify, how FSAs differ, and why to ask a tax advisor first.

item.title: Does Medicare cover concierge medicine?
item.description: Medicare does not pay concierge membership fees, but it still covers your visits and tests. Here is how assignment works and what gets billed to Medicare.

item.title: Concierge medicine and direct primary care are not the same
item.description: Concierge medicine and direct primary care both charge a membership, but they differ on insurance billing, fee structure, Florida law and the new HSA rule.

item.title: Concierge medicine vs. MDVIP: how the models differ
item.description: How a national affiliate network like MDVIP differs from an independent concierge practice, and the questions worth asking before you join either one.
